docs.title: midigpt
docs.text:
GPT-2 transformer for controllable, multitrack symbolic music generation.

  • Fill in missing bars while preserving your existing arrangement
  • Generate new tracks from scratch, conditioned on musical attributes
  • Steer the output by controlling note density, polyphony, and note duration — globally or per bar
  • Integrate with your DAW via a real-time OSC server
  • One-line setup — load pretrained models from HuggingFace Hub, no compiler needed

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
pip install "midigpt[inference]"

from midigpt import Score, Track, Bar
from midigpt.inference import InferenceEngine, GenerationRequest, InferenceConfig, TrackPrompt

engine = InferenceEngine.from_pretrained("yellow_medium")

# 4-bar score with one empty melodic track
score = Score(tracks=[Track(bars=[Bar() for _ in range(4)])])

result = engine.session(
    score,
    GenerationRequest(
        tracks=[TrackPrompt(id=0, bars=[0, 1, 2, 3])],
        config=InferenceConfig(model_dim=4, mask_mode="attention"),
    ),
).run()

total = sum(len(b.notes) for t in result.tracks for b in t.bars)
print(f"Generated {total} notes")
result.to_midi("output.mid")

The model is downloaded once and cached by huggingface_hub in ~/.cache/huggingface/hub/.

docs.title: InferenceEngine
docs.text:
from midigpt.inference import InferenceEngine

Top-level entry point. Owns the model, tokenizer, and attribute analyzer.

docs.title: InferenceEngine.from_pretrained
docs.text:
@classmethod
def from_pretrained(
    cls,
    name: str,
    hf_repo: str = "Metacreation/MIDI-GPT",
    analyzer: AttributeAnalyzer | None = None,
    device: str | None = None,
    token: str | None = None,
) -> InferenceEngine

name is the checkpoint filename prefix on the repo, e.g. yellow_medium, prism_medium, expressive_medium. The actual filename is resolved dynamically — prefers <name>-final.safetensors, falls back to the highest-step snapshot. Downloads and caches via huggingface_hub; when the Hub can't be reached or refuses the download, a cached copy is used (with a warning). device: "cuda", "mps", "cpu", or "auto" (CUDA if available, else MPS, else CPU). The default, None, loads the model on the CPU.

token is a Hugging Face access token, for a gated repo (see Models — access tokens). When None, the token from HF_TOKEN or hf auth login is used. A gated repo with no access and nothing cached raises PermissionError, saying how to get access.

engine = InferenceEngine.from_pretrained("yellow_medium")
engine = InferenceEngine.from_pretrained("prism_medium", hf_repo="myorg/myrepo", device="cuda")
engine = InferenceEngine.from_pretrained("prism_medium", token="hf_...")

docs.title: controls keys
docs.text:
Check a checkpoint's supports_* capabilities (GET /info — see HTTP Server) before relying on any of these; not every model supports every control.

Key Type Description time_signature int Index into encoder_config.time_signatures pitch_mask dict Restrict/shape which pitches this track's NoteOnset tokens may sample. Hard allow-set (pick one): {"pitches": [60, 62, 64]} (exact MIDI pitches), {"scale": "major", "root": 0} (preset name + pitch class 0–11), or {"pitch_classes": [0, 2, 4, 5, 7, 9, 11]} (any octave). Optional soft reweight layered on top: "shape": {"type": "uniform", "min": 48, "max": 72} or "shape": {"type": "normal", "mean": 60, "std": 8} rhythm_mask dict Restrict/shape which within-bar tick this track's TimeAbsolutePos tokens may land on. Mutually exclusive (pick one): "positions" — hard exact rhythm, forces the onset grid and polyphony exactly ([{"pos": 0, "polyphony": 1}, {"pos": 24, "polyphony": 2}]; first entry must be pos=0; requires config.tracks_per_step == 1, and "auto" becomes 1), or "grid" — soft grid-granularity bias ({"unit": "eighth", "strength": 0.8}; unit: whole/half/quarter/eighth/sixteenth/quarter_triplet/eighth_triplet/sixteenth_triplet; strength 1.0 = hard-quantize, 0.0 = no bias) remix dict Regenerate this track's bars as a partial variation of content already on score for those bars, instead of generating fresh. The onset schedule (which ticks have notes, how many per tick) is always reproduced exactly from the reference — only note-level values are eligible for resampling. {"amount": 0.3, "mode": "pitch"}: amount is the fraction of eligible note-attributes resampled (0–1); mode: "pitch" — only pitch is eligible, duration stays exact ("vary notes, keep the rhythm"); mode: "full" — pitch and duration are each independently eligible. Velocity is always left to free sampling in both modes

Controls the step planner and sampling pipeline.

docs.title: Step planner
docs.text: Field Type Default Description model_dim int or "auto" 4 Context window size in bars — must be in the checkpoint's num_bars_map. "auto": the largest one the piece fills bars_per_step int or "auto" 1 AR: new bars per step (the rest of the window is the track's own history). Infill: the span of target bars one step covers. "auto": AR keeps max(min_overlap_bars, ar_overlap × model_dim) bars of history; infill takes a whole window tracks_per_step int or "auto" 1 Infill tracks generated together (AR is always one track per step). "auto": all of them ar_overlap float 0.5 "auto" bars_per_step, AR: the share of the window kept as history min_overlap_bars int 2 "auto" bars_per_step, AR: at least this many bars of history context str "auto" When a step would not fit the model (prompt + budget_margin × its estimated output), whole context tracks are left out of the request: "auto" drops context_drop first, then the tracks the model attends to least (attention from the end of the prompt, top layers, per token; a role table when the prompt is too long to read); "listed" drops only context_drop; "all" never drops. Then, for what the request leaves "auto": fewer infill tracks per step, then fewer bars per step (each halved). The window steps down only when all of that is not enough context_drop list[int] [] Tracks to drop first, in this order context_keep list[int] [] Tracks never dropped (targets never are) budget_margin float 1.25 Safety factor on the estimated output tokens plan_only bool false Return the plan (windows and the bars each step writes) without generating; /generate answers {"status": "planned", "model_dim", "plan": [...], "dropped_context"} (see HTTP Server), and SamplingSession.plan_summary() returns the same plan shuffle bool false Run the infill steps in random order, seeded by the request seed; AR steps keep their order, each continuing the last mask_mode str "token" How to represent future bars: "token", "attention", "attention_approx", "attention_skip", "remove"

docs.title: Sampling
docs.text: Field Type Default Description temperature float 1.0 Softmax temperature — higher is more random top_k int 0 Keep top-k highest-probability tokens (0 = off) top_p float 1.0 Nucleus: keep the smallest set summing to ≥ top_p (1.0 = off) mask_k int 0 Remove the top-k most-likely tokens for novelty (0 = off) mask_p float 0.0 Anti-nucleus: remove tokens summing to ≥ mask_p from the top (0.0 = off)

docs.title: Retries and quality checks
docs.text: Field Type Default Description max_attempts int 3 Maximum sampling retries per step temperature_escalation float 1.0 Multiply temperature by this factor on each retry silence_check bool True Reject steps that produce zero notes novelty_check bool True Reject steps that reproduce the original bars (see novelty_threshold) novelty_threshold float 1.0 With novelty_check, reject a step whose generated bars share at least this fraction of their (pitch, onset) notes with the original; velocity, duration and microtiming don't count. 1.0 rejects only an unchanged result seed int -1 Fix the RNG for reproducibility (-1 = free-running)

docs.title: Hard limits
docs.text: Field Type Default Description polyphony_hard_limit int 0 Reject tokens that would exceed this simultaneous-note count (0 = off) density_hard_limit int 0 Reject tokens that would exceed this notes-per-bar count (0 = off)

docs.title: Candidates
docs.text: Field Type Default Description num_candidates int 1 Independent full generations from the same prompt (one seed each), no accept/reject filtering — see SamplingSession.run_variations. Not the same as max_attempts, which retries the same candidate on rejection batch_attempts bool false Run the max_attempts retries as one batched forward pass. Not recommended: measured slower, since every retry runs a full step infill_probability float 1.0 Infill only: generate round(p × N) of the N infill target bars (at least 1), chosen at random with the request seed; the others stay as they are and act as context. AR targets are never dropped. SamplingSession.generated_bars lists the bars picked

docs.title: SamplingSession.run_variations
docs.text:
def run_variations(self) -> list

config.num_candidates independent full generations from the same prompt — one seed per candidate, no accept/reject filtering (unlike the max_attempts retry loop). For "give me a few takes, I'll pick one" workflows. Returns a list of {"score": Score | None, "seed": int, "gen_count": int, "error": str | None, "truncated": bool} dicts, one per candidate — score is None and error is set for a candidate that failed.

docs.title: SamplingSession.cancel_event
docs.text:

Set this (or assign an Event and .set() it from another thread) to stop an in-flight run()/run_variations() mid-decode — it raises GenerationCancelled carrying whatever was generated so far. Used by the HTTP server's POST /generate/{request_id}/cancel; see HTTP Server — Cancellation.

docs.title: RequestValidationError
docs.text:
from midigpt.inference import RequestValidationError

Raised by InferenceEngine.session() when the request is structurally invalid — e.g. a bar index out of range, an unknown attribute name, a model_dim not in the checkpoint's map, or mask_mode="token" on an encoder that lacks MaskBar.

docs.title: GenerationCancelled
docs.text:
from midigpt.inference import GenerationCancelled

Raised by SamplingSession.run()/run_variations() when cancel_event is observed set mid-decode. Carries whatever was generated before the cancellation, decoded through the same path a natural completion would use: exc.partial is a Score (from run()) or the same list of per-candidate dicts run_variations() normally returns (from run_variations()); exc.gen_count is how many tokens were generated before the cancel.

docs.title: Attribute Controls — Implementation Guide
docs.text: This document explains every step required to add a new attribute control to MIDI-GPT, from the C++ token type through the Python class to model configuration and inference.

docs.title: What is an attribute control?
docs.text:
An attribute control is a single token prepended to a track or bar in the token stream that steers the model toward a target musical property (density, polyphony, key, etc.). The model learns to condition on these tokens during training; at inference time you can set them to any value in their domain to guide generation.

There are two levels:

Level Token position One value per "track" Before the first Bar token of a track Entire track (generation window) "bar" After each Bar token Individual bar

docs.title: Overview of the pipeline
docs.text:
types.h enum           → integer ID for this token type
encoder_config.cpp     → from_string() resolves "Name" → enum value
add_attribute_token_domains() → extends vocab with (name, size) pairs
Python BaseAttribute   → compute() + quantize() + metadata
ATTRIBUTE_REGISTRY     → maps "registry_key" → class
TOKEN_TYPE_TO_ATTRIBUTE→ maps C++ name → (registry_key, params)
AttributeAnalyzer      → orchestrates compute/quantize, builds constraints
BarAttributeValueConstraint / AttributeValueConstraint → enforce at inference
decoder.cpp            → reads emitted tokens back into track.attributes

docs.title: 1. Add to the C++ TokenType enum
docs.text:
File: src/cpp/core/types.h

Pick the next available integer and add an enumerator:

MyNewAttribute = 85,

Rules: - The integer is permanent once a model is trained on it — do not reuse or reorder. - Check from_string() in encoder_config.cpp to see which names are already registered; add the new name there if it is missing (see step 2). - Avoid creating aliases to existing integers unless you intend to reuse the same vocabulary slot.

docs.title: 2. Register the name in from_string() / to_string()
docs.text:
File: src/cpp/tokenizer/encoder_config.cpp

Find the from_string switch and add:

if (s == "MyNewAttribute") return TokenType::MyNewAttribute;

And the reverse in to_string:

case TokenType::MyNewAttribute: return "MyNewAttribute";

This is the exact string Python must use as token_type. A mismatch causes a std::runtime_error at vocab-build time.

docs.title: 3. Wire the token into encoder.cpp
docs.text:
File: src/cpp/tokenizer/encoder.cpp

The encoder pulls quantized values out of track.attributes and emits them as tokens. You must register your attribute in one of two places depending on its level. Skipping this step is silent: Python will compute the value, the decoder will know how to read it back, but no token will ever reach the model.

Track-level: extend the post_inst_attrs table (in the per-track loop, after the Instrument token):

const std::vector<std::pair<std::string, TokenType>> post_inst_attrs = {
    {"min_polyphony",     TokenType::MinPolyphony},
    ...
    {"my_new_attribute",  TokenType::MyNewAttribute},  // ← add here
};

The string key MUST equal the Python class's name field. The vocab_.has(type) and track.attributes.count(key) guards mean: nothing is emitted when the model's vocab doesn't include the type, or when Python didn't compute a value for this track.

Bar-level: extend the bar_attrs table inside the per-bar loop:

const std::vector<std::pair<std::string, TokenType>> bar_attrs = {
    {"bar_Tension_" + idx_str,       TokenType::Tension},
    ...
    {"bar_MyNewAttribute_" + idx_str, TokenType::MyNewAttribute},  // ← add here
};

The bar-level key convention is "bar_<TokenType_string>_<bar_idx>" — using the exact string from to_string(TokenType), NOT the Python name. This must match what the decoder writes (step 4) so that encode → decode → encode is a fixed point.

If your attribute differentiates per track type (e.g. Tension for melodic, TensionDrum for drums), add BOTH bar-key/TokenType pairs — the encoder simply emits whichever key the Python side populated, and Python's track-type filter ensures only one is populated per track.

docs.title: 4. Handle the token in decoder.cpp
docs.text:
File: src/cpp/tokenizer/decoder.cpp

Add a case in the main switch. For track-level attributes:

case TokenType::MyNewAttribute:
    if (current_track) current_track->attributes["my_new_attribute"] = value;
    break;

For bar-level attributes:

case TokenType::MyNewAttribute:
    if (current_track && current_bar_idx >= 0)
        current_track->attributes[
            "bar_MyNewAttribute_" + std::to_string(current_bar_idx)
        ] = value;
    break;

The string key must match the Python attribute's name field (track-level) or follow the "bar_{token_type}_{bar_idx}" convention (bar-level). This is what enables the encode → decode → encode fixed-point and powers AttributeAnalyzer.report().

docs.title: 5. Write the Python attribute class
docs.text:
File: create or extend a file in src/python/midigpt/attributes/

Inherit from BaseAttribute:

from midigpt._types import Score
from midigpt.attributes.base import BaseAttribute


class MyNewAttribute(BaseAttribute):
    size = 8  # number of discrete bins (vocab domain size)

    def __init__(self, level: str = "track", track_type: str = "melodic"):
        self.level = level
        self.track_type = track_type  # "melodic" | "drum" | "both"
        self.name = ("bar_" if level == "bar" else "") + "my_new_attribute"
        self.token_type = "MyNewAttribute"  # must match C++ from_string() exactly

    def compute(self, score: Score, track_idx: int, bar_idx: int | None = None) -> float | int:
        # Return a raw (un-quantized) value.
        # When level == "bar" and bar_idx is not None, scope to that bar only.
        track = score.tracks[track_idx]
        ...
        return raw_value

    def quantize(self, value: float | int) -> int:
        # Map raw value into [0, size-1].
        return max(0, min(self.size - 1, int(value)))

    def value_labels(self) -> list[str]:
        # Optional: human-readable label for each bin — used by UIs.
        return [f"level {i}" for i in range(self.size)]

Key contracts: - compute() must work for both track-level (no bar_idx) and bar-level (with bar_idx) if your class supports both levels. - quantize() must return a valid index in [0, size - 1]. - token_type must be the exact string returned by C++ to_string(). - name is the dict key used in track.attributes (decoder → Python).

docs.title: 6. Register in __init__.py
docs.text:
File: src/python/midigpt/attributes/__init__.py

ATTRIBUTE_REGISTRY — maps a short key (used in attribute_controls_json configs) to the class:

from midigpt.attributes.my_new_attribute import MyNewAttribute

ATTRIBUTE_REGISTRY = {
    ...
    "my_new_attribute": MyNewAttribute,
}

TOKEN_TYPE_TO_ATTRIBUTE — maps the C++ token type name to (registry_key, constructor_params). This is used by AttributeAnalyzer.from_config() to auto-wire attributes when loading a checkpoint whose token_domains contains this token type:

TOKEN_TYPE_TO_ATTRIBUTE = {
    ...
    "MyNewAttribute": ("my_new_attribute", {}),
    # Or with params:  ("my_new_attribute", {"level": "bar"}),
}

Add the class to __all__ as well.

docs.title: 7. Configure a model to use it
docs.text:
In an encoder config JSON, add the attribute to attribute_controls_json:

{
  "attribute_controls_json": [
    {"name": "my_new_attribute", "params": {"level": "track", "track_type": "melodic"}}
  ]
}

Or, if the model's token_domains already includes "MyNewAttribute", from_config() auto-instantiates it with default params via TOKEN_TYPE_TO_ATTRIBUTE — no explicit attribute_controls_json needed.

docs.title: 8. Use it at inference
docs.text:
from midigpt.inference import GenerationRequest, InferenceConfig, TrackPrompt

tp = TrackPrompt(
    id=0,
    bars=[0, 1, 2, 3],
    attributes={"my_new_attribute": 5},  # track-level: bin index 0..size-1
    # bar_attributes={0: {"my_new_attribute": 3}},  # bar-level
)
request = GenerationRequest(tracks=[tp], config=InferenceConfig(model_dim=4, mask_mode="attention"))
result = engine.session(score, request).run()

The validation layer checks: - Value is in range [0, size-1] - Track-level attributes go in tp.attributes, bar-level in tp.bar_attributes (wrong placement raises ValueError) - achievable_range() is called to warn (not reject) when a target is physically infeasible given the fixed bars

docs.title: 9. Inspect results with report()
docs.text:
After generation, compare what the model sampled against what the notes actually encode:

analyzer = AttributeAnalyzer.from_config(encoder_config)
report = analyzer.report(result_score, track_idx=0, requested=tp.attributes)

for attr_name, entry in report["track"].items():
    print(attr_name, entry)
# {"sampled": 5, "realized": 4, "requested": 5, "consistent": False, "achieved": False}

for bar_idx, bar_entry in enumerate(report["bars"]):
    print(bar_idx, bar_entry)
  • sampled: token value the model emitted (written by decoder into track.attributes)
  • realized: value computed from the actual generated notes
  • requested: the value you asked for (if you passed requested=)
  • consistent: sampled == realized — True means the model's token accurately describes its own output
  • achieved: realized == requested — True means generation hit the target

docs.title: Notes on aliases and disambiguation
docs.text:
Several token types share an integer with a shorter alias defined in types.h. These are intentional — the alias is the canonical Python-facing name, and the longer name describes the architectural role:

Canonical alias Full name Integer OnsetPolyphony BarLevelOnsetPolyphonyMax 42 PitchClassSet BarLevelPitchClassSet 51 SilenceProportion TrackLevelSilenceProportionMax 53 PitchRange TrackLevelPitchRangeMax 49 NoteDurationDist NoteDuration 26

Because OnsetPolyphony = 42 is the same integer as BarLevelOnsetPolyphonyMax, the decoder uses token position to disambiguate: a token 42 before the first Bar in a track writes "onset_polyphony" (track-level); after a Bar token it writes "bar_BarLevelOnsetPolyphonyMax_N" (bar-level).

Do not introduce new aliases. Bar-level and track-level variants of the same concept need distinct integers (e.g. BarLevelOnsetDensity = 40 vs TrackLevelOnsetDensity = 43).

docs.title: Token types with no C++ entry yet
docs.text:
These Python classes exist and work for compute/quantize but cannot be injected into the model vocab until a C++ token type is assigned:

  • SilenceProportion(level="bar") — token_type "SilenceProportionBar" (no C++ enum entry)
  • NoteDurationQuantile(level="bar") — token_type "MinNoteDurationBar" / "MaxNoteDurationBar" (no C++ enum entry)
  • PitchClassSet(level="track") — token_type "PitchClassSetTrack" (no C++ enum entry)

They are excluded from TOKEN_TYPE_TO_ATTRIBUTE and will not be auto-inferred from checkpoints until corresponding C++ types are added.

docs.title: The composer's view
docs.text:
From a composer's perspective, midigpt is a collaborator you can hand a piece of music to and say: "fill in these bars" or "write a new track from scratch". You describe what you want — which bars to generate, how dense the notes should be, how much polyphony — and the model produces music that fits the surrounding context.

Under the hood, this involves breaking your request into a sequence of generation steps and running the language model once per step. Understanding steps is the key to understanding every control parameter in InferenceConfig.

docs.title: The step planner
docs.text:
When you call engine.session(score, request).run(), the step planner (midigpt.inference.planner) analyses your GenerationRequest and produces an ordered list of steps. Each step is one independent forward pass through the model.

flowchart TD
    A["score + GenerationRequest"] --> B["step planner"]
    B --> C["Step 1"]
    B --> D["Step 2"]
    B --> E["Step N"]
    C --> F["encode context window"]
    F --> G["GPT-2 forward pass"]
    G --> H["apply grammar + constraint mask"]
    H --> I["sample one token"]
    I --> J{"step\ncomplete?"}
    J -- no --> F
    J -- yes --> K["decode tokens → bars"]
    K --> L["next step"]
    L --> D

The planner decides:

  • How many steps — in an order that lets each step use the output of previous ones as context: AR tracks first, one at a time, then infill.
  • Which bars are in the context window — a window of model_dim bars placed on the targets, not on a grid from bar 0. An AR step keeps model_dim − bars_per_step bars of the track's own history before the bars it writes and writes up to the window's right edge (so the first window from bar 0 is written whole), then the window slides by bars_per_step. An infill step's window is centred on its chunk of target bars.
  • How many infill tracks to generate together — controlled by tracks_per_step. An AR step always generates one track.
  • The order of the infill steps — the planner's order, or a random one with shuffle=True (seeded by the request seed).

model_dim, bars_per_step and tracks_per_step each also take "auto": the largest window the piece fills; for AR, max(min_overlap_bars, ar_overlap × model_dim) bars of history per step, for infill a whole window; every infill track at once. Pass plan_only=True to see the plan without generating.

docs.title: The context window
docs.text:
Every step encodes a fixed-width slice of the score. That slice is model_dim bars wide and contains every track not marked ignore (unless context fitting leaves some out, see below).

Within the window, each bar plays one of three roles:

Role What it contains How it's encoded Context Real notes — either the original content or bars already generated by a previous step Full token sequence Target The bar(s) to be generated in this step Empty — the model fills these in Masked Future bars that will be generated in a later step Represented according to mask_mode

A typical infill window looks like this:

◀────────────── model_dim bars ──────────────▶

  bar 0       bar 1       bar 2       bar 3
┌──────────┬──────────┬──────────┬──────────┐
│ CONTEXT  │ CONTEXT  │  TARGET  │  MASKED  │
│ (notes)  │ (notes)  │ (empty)  │(future?) │
└──────────┴──────────┴──────────┴──────────┘

The model sees context bars, predicts the target bar, and the masked bars are hidden so it cannot "cheat" by looking ahead.

docs.title: model_dim — musical context size
docs.text:
model_dim is not an architecture parameter. It is the number of bars the model sees in each step. Every pretrained checkpoint was trained on specific window sizes, recorded in num_bars_map — you must pass a model_dim value that appears in that list.

A larger model_dim gives the model more musical context (useful for long-range phrasing) but costs more memory and is slower. A smaller value is faster and works well for local texture generation.

docs.title: tracks_per_step
docs.text: How many infill target tracks are generated in the same step. Every non-ignored track is in the window as context either way; generating tracks together lets them respond to each other, at the cost of more tokens per step. The default is 1; "auto" generates every infill track at once. AR is always one track per step.

docs.title: bars_per_step
docs.text: How many target bars are generated in a single step. A value of 1 gives the model maximum context around each bar but requires more steps. A higher value generates multiple bars in one forward pass at the cost of less surrounding context per bar.

docs.title: When a request doesn't fit
docs.text:
Before generating, each step is checked against the model's context length: its prompt plus budget_margin × its estimated output must fit. When it doesn't:

  1. Whole context tracks are left out (config.context): "auto" drops the tracks in context_drop first, then the ones the model attends to least; "listed" drops only context_drop; "all" never drops. Tracks in context_keep, and target tracks, are never dropped.
  2. For what the request left "auto", fewer infill tracks per step, then fewer bars per step.
  3. Only then does the window (model_dim) step down, keeping the steps already done.

The tracks left out are reported as SamplingSession.dropped_context (and dropped_context in the HTTP response).

docs.title: Masking strategies
docs.text:
The key design question for any generative model with infill is: how should the model represent bars it has not yet generated?

midigpt offers five strategies, set via InferenceConfig(mask_mode=...).

docs.title: "token" — explicit mask token
docs.text:
The encoder emits a special MaskBar token for each masked bar. The model is trained to understand this as "a bar will appear here but its content is unknown". This is the most explicit signal but requires the encoder vocabulary to include a MaskBar domain.

[ CONTEXT ] [ CONTEXT ] [ TARGET ] [ MaskBar ] [ MaskBar ]

Only available on models trained with MaskBar support. No released checkpoint currently has this.

docs.title: "attention" — exact span masking
docs.text:
Masked bars are encoded normally but their positions are zeroed in the KV cache after the prefill step — the model physically cannot attend to them. This is precise and works on any encoder.

[ CONTEXT ] [ CONTEXT ] [ TARGET ] [ encoded | zeroed in KV ]

docs.title: "attention_approx" — approximate span masking
docs.text: A single attention mask is applied at prefill covering all masked positions, and the KV cache is surgically trimmed after. Cheaper than exact masking for long sequences.

docs.title: "attention_skip" — filtered input
docs.text: Tokens for masked bars are removed from the input sequence entirely and position_ids are passed explicitly so the model maintains correct positional awareness. Lightest on compute.

docs.title: "remove" — omit entirely
docs.text: Masked bars are not included in the token stream at all. The simplest approach and the one with the shortest sequences, but gives the model no signal about where future bars will fall.

docs.title: Infill vs. autoregressive
docs.text:
These two modes differ in where target bars sit relative to context:

Infill — target bars are surrounded by context on both sides. The model fills a gap.

[ CONTEXT ] [ CONTEXT ] [ TARGET ] [ TARGET ] [ CONTEXT ] [ CONTEXT ]

Autoregressive — target bars extend past the end of any existing content. The model generates forward in time.

[ CONTEXT ] [ CONTEXT ] [ CONTEXT ] [ TARGET ] [ TARGET ] [ TARGET ]
                                       ← generated left to right →

In AR mode there are no future bars to mask, so mask_mode has no effect. The model generates the next bar given everything before it, one bar (or one step) at a time.

docs.title: Putting it together
docs.text:
When you build a GenerationRequest, you are telling the planner:

  • Which bars to generate (TrackPrompt.bars) — these become targets.
  • Which bars to ignore (TrackPrompt.ignore) — these are excluded entirely.
  • Which bars to hide (TrackPrompt.mask_bars) — these are always masked regardless of mode.
  • How wide the context window should be (InferenceConfig.model_dim).
  • How to represent unknowns (InferenceConfig.mask_mode).
  • What musical character to aim for (TrackPrompt.attributes and TrackPrompt.bar_attributes).

The planner turns those instructions into the minimal set of steps required to generate all requested bars, scheduling them so earlier steps' output feeds into later steps' context.

docs.title: Architecture notes
docs.text:
A few things worth knowing before modifying the code:

  • Guides for extending tokenization/conditioning:
  • For implementing a new attribute control end-to-end, follow the Attribute Controls Guide.
  • For designing and validating encoder configurations, follow the Encoder Config Guide.
  • Token IDs and vocabularies live exclusively in C++. EncoderConfig.from_json(str) is the entry point. Tokenizer.vocab_size() is authoritative — do not recompute it from sum(token_domains[*].domain_size).
  • _types.Score vs. _core.Score: The Python side uses _types.Score (dataclasses). The C++ bindings use _core.Score. _converters.to_cpp() and from_cpp() convert between them. SamplingSession._run_step() normalises to _types.Score on entry.
  • model_dim is a generation-window parameter, not a score bar count. Tests that use small scores must pad to at least model_dim bars.
  • cibuildwheel on Windows: cmd.exe does not strip single quotes. The test-command in pyproject.toml must use TOML literal-string outer with double quotes inside.

docs.title: Encoder Config — Design Guide
docs.text: This document explains every field in an encoder config JSON, how to design a new encoder from scratch, and the relationships between the JSON, the C++ tokenizer, and the Python attribute pipeline.

docs.title: What is an encoder config?
docs.text:
An encoder config defines a MIDI-GPT model's vocabulary and conditioning signals. It controls:

  • Which token types exist and how many discrete values each can take
  • Which musical attributes the Python side computes (density, polyphony, pitch class, etc.) and at what granularity (bar vs. track)
  • Genre conditioning (canonical genre labels and their aliases)
  • Structural tokenization parameters (resolution, time signatures, bar lengths)

A trained model is permanently bound to the encoder it was trained with. Changing any field that affects vocabulary size or token ID assignment invalidates a checkpoint.

docs.title: File location and naming
docs.text:
Encoder configs live in models/. Name them <name>_encoder.json. The <name> is used as a handle everywhere (training configs, CLI flags, checkpoint metadata).

Existing encoders: - models/yellow_encoder.json — 5 track-level attributes, no genre - models/prism_encoder.json — 9 attributes (bar + track level), 18-genre control

docs.title: token_domains
docs.text:
Required. Not inferred. Defines the vocabulary — every token type the encoder emits, and the number of distinct values it can take. Order matters: token IDs are assigned sequentially across domains.

"token_domains": [
  { "type": "PieceStart",    "domain_size": 2   },
  { "type": "Genre",         "domain_size": 18  },
  { "type": "Track",         "domain_size": 2   },
  { "type": "TrackEnd",      "domain_size": 1   },
  { "type": "Bar",           "domain_size": 1   },
  { "type": "BarEnd",        "domain_size": 1   },
  { "type": "TimeSig",       "domain_size": 36  },
  { "type": "Instrument",    "domain_size": 109 },
  { "type": "NumBars",       "domain_size": 2   },
  { "type": "NoteOnset",     "domain_size": 128 },
  { "type": "NoteDuration",  "domain_size": 96  },
  { "type": "TimeAbsolutePos","domain_size": 192 },
  { "type": "VelocityLevel", "domain_size": 32  },
  { "type": "FillInPlaceholder","domain_size": 1 },
  { "type": "FillInStart",   "domain_size": 1   },
  { "type": "FillInEnd",     "domain_size": 1   }
]

The first 16 entries above are required for all encoders. Attribute tokens are appended after them.

Critical rules: - domain_size for an attribute token must exactly match the Python attribute class's size field — there is no automatic check. - Genre must appear before Track (it is a piece-level token). If genre_groups is omitted, omit Genre from token_domains too. - Adding or reordering entries changes all subsequent token IDs. Only add to the end, or accept that the checkpoint is incompatible. - "type" strings must match the C++ TokenType enum exactly (see attribute_controls_guide.md for the full list of registered names).

Attribute token domain sizes (from Python BaseAttribute.size):

Token type Domain size Level Python class NoteDensity 10 track NoteDensityQuantile MinPolyphony 10 track PolyphonyQuantile(mode="min") MaxPolyphony 10 track PolyphonyQuantile(mode="max") MinNoteDuration 6 track NoteDurationQuantile(mode="min") MaxNoteDuration 6 track NoteDurationQuantile(mode="max") SilenceProportion 10 track SilenceProportion PitchRange 128 track PitchRange KeySignature 25 track KeySignature OnsetPolyphony 10 track OnsetPolyphony PitchClassSetTrack 13 track PitchClassSet(level="track") TrackLevelNomml 13 track Nomml BarLevelOnsetDensity 10 bar NoteDensityQuantile(level="bar") BarLevelOnsetPolyphonyMin 10 bar PolyphonyQuantile(mode="min", level="bar") BarLevelOnsetPolyphonyMax 10 bar PolyphonyQuantile(mode="max", level="bar") PitchClassSet 13 bar PitchClassSet Tension 10 bar Tension TensionDrum 10 bar TensionDrum Genre N piece genre_grouping.num_genres() UseVelocity 2 piece (structural switch: 0=no, 1=yes) UseMicrotiming 2 piece (structural switch: 0=no, 1=yes)

Note: PitchClassSetTrack has no C++ entry yet — it cannot be used in token_domains until one is added. See attribute_controls_guide.md § "Token types with no C++ entry yet".

docs.title: attribute_controls
docs.text:
Tells the Python AttributeAnalyzer which attributes to compute during training and encoding. Each entry must have a corresponding token_domains entry with the correct domain size.

"attribute_controls": [
  { "name": "key_signature" },
  { "name": "silence_proportion" },
  { "name": "pitch_range" },
  { "name": "note_duration_quantile", "params": { "mode": "min" } },
  { "name": "note_duration_quantile", "params": { "mode": "max" } },
  { "name": "note_density_quantile",  "params": { "level": "bar" } },
  { "name": "polyphony_quantile",     "params": { "mode": "min", "level": "bar" } },
  { "name": "polyphony_quantile",     "params": { "mode": "max", "level": "bar" } },
  { "name": "pitch_class_set" }
]

name is a key in ATTRIBUTE_REGISTRY (src/python/midigpt/attributes/__init__.py). params are passed as constructor kwargs to the Python attribute class.

Bar vs. track level:

Level Specify Token type used Token position in sequence track (default) no level param e.g. NoteDensity Once, before first bar of each track bar "level": "bar" e.g. BarLevelOnsetDensity Once per bar, after Bar token

Bar-level attributes increase sequence length by num_bars × num_tracks tokens. They give the model fine-grained per-bar control at the cost of longer contexts. Prefer bar-level for attributes that vary meaningfully within a piece (density, polyphony, harmony); prefer track-level for global characteristics (key, range, silence).

The token_domains entry must match the level. A note_density_quantile without level param expects NoteDensity in token_domains; with "level": "bar" it expects BarLevelOnsetDensity. There is no runtime error if they mismatch — the C++ will silently emit nothing.

docs.title: genre_groups
docs.text:
Optional. Enables piece-level genre conditioning. If present, add Genre to token_domains with domain_size equal to the number of canonical genre keys.

"genre_groups": {
  "rock":  ["rock"],
  "metal": ["metal", "heavy metal", "grunge", "hardcore"],
  "pop":   ["pop", "k pop", "dance", "disco"]
}

Format rules: - Keys are canonical genre names — these are what the model learns and what inference accepts. - Values are alias lists — raw strings (from the dataset) that map to that canonical name. Lookup is case-insensitive. An alias may appear in only one group. - Canonical names self-register automatically. The C++ GenreGrouping always adds the canonical key to its lookup table regardless of whether it appears in the alias list. So encode("rock") works even if "rock" is not listed under "rock". You do not need to repeat the key in its own alias list. - Unknown genres are silently skipped during training. _genre_token() calls contains() before encode() — dataset rows with genres not in any alias list simply emit no genre token (genre = -1). The C++ encode() would throw for unknown genres, but training never reaches it. - Dense IDs are assigned in alphabetical key order — metal = 0, pop = 1, rock = 2 in the example above. Token ID assignment is fixed once training begins. - domain_size in token_domains must equal the number of keys.

GigaMIDI specifics:

The genre field in GigaMIDI v2.0.0 is music_style_scraped. It is a URL-encoded, comma-separated string:

"alternative-indie%2cpop%2crock"  →  ["alternative-indie", "pop", "rock"]

The Python dataset reads it as: 

from urllib.parse import unquote
genres = [g.strip() for g in unquote(raw).split(",") if g.strip()]
known = [g for g in genres if genre_grouping.contains(g)]
# randomly sample one known genre per training example

Coverage for the prism_encoder.json mapping (18 canonical genres, 18M genre-labeled rows in GigaMIDI v2.0.0 train): 99.9% of labeled rows map to a known canonical genre. Only ~6% of all rows have any genre label.

docs.title: resolution
docs.text:
Ticks per quarter note for the tokenization grid. Controls the finest time granularity the model can represent.

"resolution": 12

Common values: 12 (default), 24 (finer grid, larger vocabulary). Higher resolution increases TimeAbsolutePos domain size and sequence length.

docs.title: decode_resolution
docs.text:
Ticks per quarter note for the output MIDI. Usually much higher than resolution (e.g. 1920) to produce standard-compliant MIDI files. The decoder up-scales token positions by decode_resolution / resolution.

"decode_resolution": 1920

docs.title: note_duration_max_beats
docs.text:
Maximum note duration in beats. Notes longer than this are clamped. Determines NoteDuration domain size indirectly.

"note_duration_max_beats": 8

docs.title: num_bars_map
docs.text:
List of valid bar-count window sizes the model is trained on. Used to set the NumBars token domain size and to configure the training sampler.

"num_bars_map": [4, 8]

This means the model sees 4-bar and 8-bar windows; domain_size for NumBars should equal the length of this list.

docs.title: time_signatures
docs.text:
Allowable time signatures as "numerator/denominator" strings. Filters out rows during preprocessing (Phase 2). Must match domain_size for TimeSig in token_domains.

"time_signatures": ["4/4", "3/4", "6/8", ...]

TimeSig domain size = len(time_signatures).

docs.title: pitch_range
docs.text:
MIDI pitch range [min, max] (inclusive). Notes outside this range are filtered during encoding.

"pitch_range": [0, 127]

docs.title: velocity_levels and velocity_sticky
docs.text:
Number of discrete velocity bins. velocity_sticky means the velocity token is only emitted when it changes (reduces sequence length).

"velocity_levels": 32,
"velocity_sticky": true

docs.title: instrument_merge_groups
docs.text:
Groups of MIDI program numbers (0-indexed) that are treated as the same instrument for tokenization. Reduces instrument vocabulary fragmentation.

"instrument_merge_groups": [[0, 1, 2], [4, 5], ...]

docs.title: supports_infill and supports_mask_bar_token
docs.text: Feature flags. supports_infill: true enables fill-in-the-blank generation (requires FillInPlaceholder, FillInStart, FillInEnd in token_domains). supports_mask_bar_token enables the MaskBar token for bar-level masking.

docs.title: emit_delta_tokens
docs.text: If true, emit time-delta tokens instead of absolute position tokens. Not used in current production encoders.

docs.title: Designing a new encoder: decisions checklist
docs.text:
1. What attributes to include?

Start from the available attribute types (table above). Ask: - Is the attribute musically meaningful at bar level or only globally? → bar vs. track - How many bins does it need? More bins = finer control but larger vocab and slower convergence. - Will the training data have good coverage? (e.g. genre is sparse in GigaMIDI — only 6% of rows are labeled)

2. Bar-level or track-level for density/polyphony?

Bar-level is recommended if you want the model to follow per-bar musical shape. Track-level is cheaper and sufficient for style-level control. Do not include both versions of the same attribute — pick one.

3. Genre groups?

Only add genre if your training data has meaningful genre coverage and you want inference-time genre control. Build the alias list from an audit of the actual dataset values (see the analysis that produced prism_encoder.json).

4. Vocabulary size budget

A rough guide: - Base tokens (structural, no attributes, no genre): ~650 tokens - Each track-level attribute: +domain_size tokens - Each bar-level attribute: +domain_size tokens (but adds tokens per bar in sequence) - Genre: +num_genres tokens

Larger vocabularies increase model size (embedding table) and may slow convergence for rare tokens.

docs.title: Validating a new encoder config
docs.text:
After writing the JSON, always validate before starting training:

import midigpt._core as _core

with open("models/my_encoder.json") as f:
    cfg = _core.EncoderConfig.from_json(f.read())

vocab = _core.Vocabulary(cfg)
print(f"vocab_size: {vocab.size()}")

# If genre_groups is present:
g = cfg.genre_grouping
print(f"num_genres: {g.num_genres()}")
print(g.encode("rock"), g.decode(0))

Errors at this stage: - std::runtime_error: Unknown token type 'Foo' → Foo is not a registered C++ TokenType name - AttributeError: 'NoneType' ... on cfg.genre_grouping → genre_groups is missing from JSON but Genre is in token_domains, or vice versa

Also verify that domain_size in token_domains matches Python attribute size:

from midigpt.attributes import ATTRIBUTE_REGISTRY

for ctrl in config["attribute_controls"]:
    cls = ATTRIBUTE_REGISTRY[ctrl["name"]]
    inst = cls(**ctrl.get("params", {}))
    print(inst.token_type, inst.size)
# Cross-check these sizes against token_domains entries

docs.title: Common pitfalls
docs.text:
attribute_controls and token_domains must both be updated. Adding an attribute to attribute_controls without a matching token_domains entry means Python computes the value but the C++ tokenizer emits nothing — silent data loss, no error.

Genre domain_size must equal the number of keys in genre_groups. The C++ reads this as a fixed-size domain at vocab-build time; a mismatch causes an out-of-range panic during encoding.

Aliases must be unique across groups. "swing" appearing in both "jazz" and "folk" causes the first-seen mapping to win silently. Audit with a deduplication check before finalizing.

PitchClassSetTrack has no C++ entry. Do not add it to token_domains — it will fail. See attribute_controls_guide.md § "Token types with no C++ entry yet".

Alphabetical key order determines genre IDs. If you rename or reorder keys after training begins, all genre tokens in the dataset's cached indices become wrong. Freeze the genre key set before running preprocess.sh.

docs.title: Examples & Controllable Generation
docs.text:
This page shows MIDI-GPT's core capabilities — Track Sampling, Bar Infilling (Inpainting) and Autoregressive Continuation — on short excerpts of freely licensed music: original pieces by Ivan Stanton released under CC0 on OpenGameArt, and public-domain scores by Beethoven and Mozart from the Mutopia Project. All examples are generated with yellow_medium.

By setting Attribute Controls (such as polyphony, note density, and note duration), you can guide the model to generate musical parts that fit your composition.

docs.title: Video Renders & MIDI Downloads
docs.text:
Each example is rendered as an MP4 video with synthesized audio and a per-track piano-roll view. Context tracks are shown in blue/green/purple, generated tracks in gold. Download links are provided for importing the .mid files into a DAW.

The examples are reproducible: python scripts/gen_doc_examples.py regenerates every MIDI file on this page (fixed seeds), and python scripts/render_doc_midi_videos.py renders the videos.

docs.title: 1. Controllable Track Sampling (Arrangement)
docs.text: Track sampling generates a completely new track conditioned on the existing ones. The new track is generated autoregressively (autoregressive=True), every other track is context (bars=[]). You can pin attribute controls to steer the new track, or leave them out and let the model sample its own controls from the prior.

docs.title: Example 1: Drums for a Rock Groove
docs.text:
We take a distortion guitar and slap bass part from Ivan Stanton's "Just Say No To Yes" (CC0) as context and generate a drum track. On yellow, note_density applies to drum tracks; adjusting it (scale 0–9) steers the drums from a sparse beat to a dense, active pattern.

Guitar & Bass Prompt (Context) Download Prompt MIDI Track Instrument Role 0 distortion_guitar Context 1 slap_bass_1 Context 2 drums Generated Sparse (note_density = 1)Medium (note_density = 3)Dense (note_density = 8)

Download Sparse Drums MIDI 

req = GenerationRequest(
    tracks=[
        TrackPrompt(id=0, bars=[]),  # distortion_guitar (context)
        TrackPrompt(id=1, bars=[]),  # slap_bass_1 (context)
        TrackPrompt(id=2, bars=[0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7], autoregressive=True,
                    attributes={"note_density": 1}),  # drums
    ],

docs.title: Example 2: A New Cello Part for a String Quartet
docs.text:
We take the two violins and the viola from the first movement of Beethoven's String Quartet Op. 18 No. 4 (public domain) and generate a new cello part, monophonic (max_polyphony = 0). Sweeping max_note_duration from index 1 (16th notes) to 4 (half notes), plus a min_note_duration = 4 (sustained) variant, gives five cello lines across the duration range. The controls shift the distribution of note lengths rather than set a hard limit, so a take can still hold a few longer notes.

docs.text:
We take the slap bass and drums from Ivan Stanton's "Savior of Humanity" (CC0) as context and generate a new distortion_guitar part in place of the original. No attribute controls are set — the model samples its own controls from the prior, giving two different guitar parts over the same groove.

Tip: When you omit attribute controls, the model draws from its learned style distribution. This is useful for exploring diverse outputs without manually specifying constraints.

docs.title: 2. Bar Infilling (Inpainting)
docs.text: Bar infilling regenerates selected bars of a track while the model blends them with the surrounding context: the bars before and after, and the other tracks.

docs.title: Example 4: Second Violin, Bars 4–7
docs.text:
We take eight bars of the first movement of Mozart's Eine kleine Nachtmusik (public domain), clear bars 4–7 of the second violin, and ask the model to infill them with a note-duration control. The first violin, viola and cello play through all 8 bars as context, and the second violin's bars 0–3 anchor the generation. The shaded region in the video marks the infilled bars.

Note: max_note_duration is a track-level attribute: it describes the whole track, including the bars that stay as they are, so in a 4-bar infill it is a soft control and not every seed follows it. The two takes below were picked from several seeds (the 16th-note one took the most tries). Track sampling (Example 2) follows the same control much more reliably.

docs.title: 3. Multi-Step Composition
docs.text: By chaining multiple generation tasks you can build up a full arrangement incrementally.

docs.title: Example 5: Multi-Step Composition
docs.text:
Starting from the first four bars of a piano, bass and strings passage from Ivan Stanton's "The Ritual" (CC0), we perform three successive generations to build a 5-track arrangement:

  1. Continuation — extend all three tracks from bar 4 to bar 7 autoregressively
  2. Track sampling — add acoustic_guitar_nylon (monophonic 16th notes)
  3. Track sampling — add drums at high density

The final video shows all five tracks. The gold tracks (guitar and drums) come from steps 2 and 3; the shaded region (bars 4–7) marks the continuation of the first three tracks.

Prompt (bars 0–3) Download Prompt MIDI All 5 Tracks (Final State) Download Final MIDI Track Instrument Role 0 acoustic_grand_piano Context (bars 0–3) + Continued (bars 4–7) 1 electric_bass_finger Context (bars 0–3) + Continued (bars 4–7) 2 string_ensemble_1 Context (bars 0–3) + Continued (bars 4–7) 3 acoustic_guitar_nylon Generated — max_polyphony = 0, max_note_duration = 1 4 drums Generated — note_density = 9 
# Step 1: continue all three tracks for bars 4-7 (one track per step, each sees the others)
step1 = GenerationRequest(
    tracks=[
        TrackPrompt(id=0, bars=[4, 5, 6, 7], autoregressive=True),  # piano
        TrackPrompt(id=1, bars=[4, 5, 6, 7], autoregressive=True),  # bass
        TrackPrompt(id=2, bars=[4, 5, 6, 7], autoregressive=True),  # strings
    ],
    config=InferenceConfig(model_dim=8, mask_mode="attention", seed=41),
)

# Step 2: add a guitar track (monophonic 16th notes) to the result of step 1
step2 = GenerationRequest(
    tracks=[
        TrackPrompt(id=0, bars=[]),  # piano (context)
        TrackPrompt(id=1, bars=[]),  # bass (context)
        TrackPrompt(id=2, bars=[]),  # strings (context)
        TrackPrompt(id=3, bars=[0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7], autoregressive=True,
                    attributes={"max_polyphony": 0, "max_note_duration": 1}),
    ],
    config=InferenceConfig(model_dim=8, mask_mode="attention", seed=42),
)

# Step 3: add drums to the result of step 2
step3 = GenerationRequest(
    tracks=[
        TrackPrompt(id=0, bars=[]),
        TrackPrompt(id=1, bars=[]),
        TrackPrompt(id=2, bars=[]),
        TrackPrompt(id=3, bars=[]),  # guitar (context)
        TrackPrompt(id=4, bars=[0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7], autoregressive=True,
                    attributes={"note_density": 9}),
    ],
    config=InferenceConfig(model_dim=8, mask_mode="attention", seed=43),
)

Before steps 2 and 3, append an empty track to the score for the new part: score.tracks.append(Track(bars=[Bar() for _ in range(8)], instrument=24)) for the nylon guitar, Track(..., track_type="drum") for the drums.

docs.title: HTTP Server
docs.text: The midigpt[http] extra adds a stateless REST API for generation. Every request carries the full score and generation parameters — the server holds no per-generation session state between calls. The persistent state is the loaded model(s) and device.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text: pip install "midigpt[http]"

docs.title: Local checkpoint
docs.text: midigpt-http --ckpt checkpoints/run_001/model_final.safetensors --port 8000

docs.title: Pretrained from HuggingFace Hub
docs.text:
# Checkpoint filename prefix on the hub (downloads once, cached in ~/.cache/huggingface/)
midigpt-http --pretrained yellow_medium --port 8000
midigpt-http --pretrained prism_medium --port 8000
midigpt-http --pretrained expressive_medium --port 8000

# Custom repo
midigpt-http --pretrained my_model --hf-repo myorg/myrepo --port 8000

docs.title: Device selection
docs.text:
The server runs on the CPU unless you pass --device, even on a machine with a GPU:

midigpt-http --pretrained yellow_medium --device cuda   # NVIDIA GPU
midigpt-http --pretrained yellow_medium --device mps    # Apple Silicon GPU
midigpt-http --pretrained yellow_medium --device auto   # CUDA if available, else MPS, else CPU
midigpt-http --pretrained yellow_medium                 # CPU (the default)

--device cuda (or mps) fails at startup if that device isn't available, rather than silently falling back to the CPU. For CUDA you need a CUDA build of PyTorch: on Linux the default pip install torch is one; on Windows it is CPU-only, so install PyTorch with the CUDA command from pytorch.org before (or after) installing midigpt. Check with:

python -c "import torch; print(torch.cuda.is_available())"   # True: --device cuda will work

With --config, set device: at the top level or per model entry (cuda, mps, auto or cpu).

docs.title: Multiple models in one server
docs.text:
Pass --config with a YAML file instead of --ckpt/--pretrained to serve several checkpoints from one process, selectable per-request via the model id:

# models.yaml
host: 0.0.0.0
port: 8000
idle_timeout: 0
max_queue: 64            # server-wide across every model
max_generation_seconds: 0
hf_repo: Metacreation/MIDI-GPT   # default for pretrained entries
hf_token: hf_...          # optional; default is HF_TOKEN / `hf auth login`
device: cuda              # default device for every entry (omit for CPU)
max_parallel: 1           # default per-model concurrency
default_model: yellow_medium     # defaults to the first entry's id if omitted

models:
  - id: yellow_medium            # the "model" id clients pass to /generate
    pretrained: yellow_medium
  - id: prism_medium
    pretrained: prism_medium
    device: cpu                 # per-entry override
    max_parallel: 2              # per-entry override — benchmark before raising, see Concurrency below
  - id: my_custom
    ckpt: /path/to/custom-final.safetensors
    hf_repo: myorg/myrepo       # per-entry override (pretrained entries only)
    hf_token: hf_...            # per-entry override (pretrained entries only)

midigpt-http --config models.yaml

host/port/idle_timeout/log_level/max_queue/max_generation_seconds in the file override the equivalent CLI flags if both are given.

hf_token is only needed for a gated repo, and only when the server's environment has no HF_TOKEN and no hf auth login; see access tokens. A gated model the server can't access stops it at startup with a message saying how to get access.

docs.title: CLI reference
docs.text:
Flag Default Description --config PATH — YAML file describing one or more models (see above). Mutually exclusive with --ckpt/--pretrained --ckpt PATH — Local .safetensors, .pt bundle, or checkpoint directory (mutually exclusive with --config/--pretrained) --pretrained NAME — Checkpoint filename prefix on HuggingFace (yellow_medium, prism_medium, expressive_medium, ...) --hf-repo REPO Metacreation/MIDI-GPT HuggingFace repo ID to download --pretrained from --device DEVICE CPU cuda, mps, cpu, or auto (CUDA if available, else MPS, else CPU) --host HOST 0.0.0.0 Bind address --port PORT 8000 TCP port --idle-timeout SECONDS 0 (off) Shut down automatically after this many seconds of inactivity --max-parallel N 1 Max concurrent /generate calls against this model (single-model mode only — use per-entry max_parallel in --config for multi-model). Each is still a full sequential decode sharing CPU/GPU with the others, not a throughput multiplier — benchmark before raising above 1 --max-queue N 64 Total requests admitted (queued + running), across all models, before returning 503 --max-generation-seconds SECONDS 0 (off) Cancel any generation that has run longer than this (time spent queued doesn't count); the response comes back "cancelled" with the partial score --log-level INFO DEBUG, INFO, WARNING, ERROR

One of --config, --ckpt, or --pretrained is required.

docs.title: Endpoints
docs.text: Interactive docs are available at http://localhost:8000/docs once the server is running.

docs.title: GET /health
docs.text:
Liveness probe (also resets the idle-shutdown timer).

{"status": "ok", "inflight": 0, "max_queue": 64}

inflight is the number of requests currently admitted (queued behind a model's concurrency limit or actively running) server-wide, across every model.

docs.title: GET /info
docs.text:
Returns capabilities/attributes/resolution for one loaded model.

GET /info?model=yellow_medium

Omit model to get the server's default model.

{
  "model": "yellow_medium",
  "default_model": "yellow_medium",
  "checkpoint": "Metacreation/MIDI-GPT/yellow_medium",
  "capabilities": {
    "tension": false,
    "note_density": true,
    "min_polyphony": true,
    "max_polyphony": true,
    "min_note_duration": true,
    "max_note_duration": true,
    "supports_token_mask": false,
    "supports_attention_mask": true,
    "supports_attention_approx": true,
    "supports_attention_skip": true,
    "supports_remove": true,
    "supports_pitch_mask": true,
    "pitch_mask_scale_presets": ["blues", "chromatic", "dorian", "..."],
    "supports_rhythm_mask": true,
    "rhythm_mask_grid_units": ["eighth", "eighth_triplet", "..."],
    "supports_remix": true,
    "supports_streaming": true,
    "model_dim_options": [4, 8],
    "max_context_tokens": 2048,
    "switchable_velocity": false,
    "switchable_microtiming": false,
    "genres": []
  },
  "attributes": {
    "note_density": 10,
    "min_polyphony": 10,
    "max_polyphony": 10,
    "min_note_duration": 6,
    "max_note_duration": 6
  },
  "attribute_track_types": {
    "note_density": "drum",
    "min_polyphony": "melodic",
    "max_polyphony": "melodic",
    "min_note_duration": "melodic",
    "max_note_duration": "melodic"
  },
  "resolution": 12
}

model_dim_options lists the window lengths (bars) the checkpoint was trained with, the valid values of config.model_dim; max_context_tokens is its context length. switchable_velocity/switchable_microtiming say whether the velocity/microtiming request controls are accepted, and genres lists the genre names it was trained with (empty when it has none). attribute_track_types says which tracks each attribute applies to ("melodic", "drum" or "both"); a request that sets an attribute on the wrong kind of track gets a 422.

The example is yellow_medium's: on yellow, note_density applies only to drum tracks, polyphony and note duration only to melodic tracks. resolution is the checkpoint's ticks per quarter note.

supports_pitch_mask/supports_rhythm_mask/supports_remix gate whether this model's checkpoint can accept the pitch_mask, rhythm_mask, and remix controls documented in API Reference — TrackPrompt — always check per model rather than assuming any two checkpoints agree.

docs.title: POST /generate
docs.text:
Generate or infill music. Pass the full score and generation parameters; receive the result score back.

Request body

{
  "score": { ... },
  "request": { ... },
  "request_id": "optional-caller-supplied-id",
  "stream": false,
  "model": "yellow_medium"
}
  • score — a Score serialised with Score.to_dict() (see Inference API)
  • request — a GenerationRequest dict (see below)
  • request_id — optional idempotency/correlation id. If omitted, the server generates one (uuid4 hex) and returns it in the response body and the X-Request-Id header. Needed to target this specific generation with POST /generate/{request_id}/cancel
  • stream — true for a text/event-stream of newly-completed notes as they're generated (see Streaming below). Not yet supported together with config.num_candidates > 1
  • model — which loaded model to run this request against (an id from GET /models). Omit to use the server's default model; single-model deployments never need to set this

Response (config.num_candidates == 1, the default)

{
  "request_id": "a1b2c3d4...",
  "model": "yellow_medium",
  "status": "completed",
  "score": { ... },
  "seed": 12345,
  "attempts": 1,
  "generated_bars": {"0": [2, 5]},
  "dropped_context": [3],
  "timing": {
    "model_forward_s": 0.42,
    "encode_s": 0.01,
    "decode_s": 0.01,
    "gen_count": 4
  },
  "tokens": {
    "context_tokens": 512,
    "generated_tokens": 128,
    "peak_context_tokens": 640,
    "max_context_tokens": 2048,
    "context_utilization": 0.25,
    "tokens_per_second": 304.76,
    "truncated": false
  }
}

generated_bars maps each generated track id to the bars it generated: the request's target bars, or the random subset config.infill_probability picked (the same for every candidate, and the same again for the same seed).

dropped_context lists the context tracks left out so every step fits the model (see config.context); empty when nothing was dropped.

attempts is how many tries the request took (1 unless a step was retried after failing novelty_check/silence_check).

status is "completed" or "cancelled" (see POST /generate/{request_id}/cancel below) — a cancelled response still carries whatever partial score was generated before the cancel was observed. context_tokens is the last step's prompt and generated_tokens the whole request's output; peak_context_tokens is the fullest the model's window got in any step (prompt plus that step's tokens). truncated: true means generation stopped because it hit the context budget, not because it reached a natural end — it may be cut off mid-bar/mid-track.

Response (config.plan_only: true)

A dry run: the request is validated and planned, nothing is generated. plan has one entry per step, in the order they would run: the window ([start, end) bars), whether it is autoregressive, and the bars it would write per track. dropped_context is what context fitting would leave out. The example is 12 bars of AR on one track with model_dim: 8 and bars_per_step: "auto".

{
  "request_id": "a1b2c3d4...",
  "model": "yellow_medium",
  "status": "planned",
  "model_dim": 8,
  "plan": [
    {"window": [0, 8], "autoregressive": true, "generate": {"0": [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7]}},
    {"window": [4, 12], "autoregressive": true, "generate": {"0": [8, 9, 10, 11]}}
  ],
  "dropped_context": []
}

Response (config.num_candidates > 1)

num_candidates independent full generations from the same prompt (one seed each, no accept/reject filtering) — for "give me a few takes, I'll pick one" workflows.

{
  "request_id": "a1b2c3d4...",
  "model": "yellow_medium",
  "status": "completed",
  "base_seed": 12345,
  "generated_bars": {"0": [2, 5]},
  "dropped_context": [],
  "candidates": [
    {"score": { ... }, "seed": 12345, "gen_count": 4, "error": null, "truncated": false},
    {"score": null, "seed": 12346, "gen_count": 0, "error": "...", "truncated": false}
  ],
  "summary": {"requested": 2, "succeeded": 1, "failed": 1, "failures": [{"seed": 12346, "reason": "..."}]},
  "timing": { ... },
  "tokens": { ... }
}

Error codes

Status Meaning 400 Malformed score/request dict, or unknown model id 422 RequestValidationError — structurally invalid generation request 500 Inference failure 503 Server busy — max_queue requests already admitted; retry after the Retry-After header (seconds)

Failed requests (500) are appended to a JSONL log for offline analysis — see MIDIGPT_FAILED_REQUESTS_LOG (default failed_requests.jsonl).

docs.title: POST /generate/{request_id}/cancel
docs.text:
Stop an in-flight generation. Returns the partial result via the original /generate call's response (streaming) or its eventual HTTP response (non-streaming), with status: "cancelled", instead of the caller having to wait for a natural finish or drop the connection.

{"request_id": "a1b2c3d4...", "status": "cancelling"}

404 if request_id has no matching in-flight request (already finished, already cancelled, or never existed).

docs.title: Streaming (stream: true)
docs.text:
Instead of one JSON response at the end, POST /generate with "stream": true returns a text/event-stream of newly-completed notes as they're generated, ending with exactly one terminal event carrying the same response shape a non-streaming call would have returned:

data: {"type": "notes", "notes": [...]}

data: {"type": "notes", "notes": [...]}

data: {"type": "done", "response": { ...same shape as the non-streaming response... }}

type is one of "notes" (a batch of newly-generated notes), "done" (completed normally), "cancelled" (stopped via the cancel endpoint or a dropped connection), or "error" ({"type": "error", "request_id": ..., "error": "..."}). Scoped to the single-candidate path — stream: true with config.num_candidates > 1 returns 400.

"notes" frames, and "progress" frames sent every 32 generated tokens between them, carry a progress object:

Field Meaning generated_tokens tokens generated so far in the whole request (every step and attempt) step_generated_tokens tokens generated in the current step context_tokens the current step's prompt max_context_tokens the model's context length model_forward_s time in the model so far attempt 1-based retry attempt of the current step

context_tokens + step_generated_tokens is the model's window in use; it never exceeds max_context_tokens. A request longer than the window runs in several steps, each with a new prompt, so generated_tokens keeps growing past it.

docs.title: Client example
docs.text:
The server accepts plain JSON — no midigpt dependency needed on the client side.

curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8000/generate \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "score": {
      "resolution": 480, "tempo": 500000,
      "tracks": [{
        "instrument": 0, "track_type": "melodic",
        "bars": [
          {"ts_numerator": 4, "ts_denominator": 4, "notes": []},
          {"ts_numerator": 4, "ts_denominator": 4, "notes": []},
          {"ts_numerator": 4, "ts_denominator": 4, "notes": []},
          {"ts_numerator": 4, "ts_denominator": 4, "notes": []}
        ]
      }]
    },
    "request": {
      "tracks": [{"id": 0, "bars": [0, 1, 2, 3]}],
      "config": {"model_dim": 4, "mask_mode": "attention"}
    }
  }'

The response score field contains the filled-in notes in the same JSON shape. mask_mode defaults to "token", which needs a MaskBar token that none of the released checkpoints has (capabilities.supports_token_mask in /info), so set one of the attention modes.

docs.title: Concurrency
docs.text:
Each model gets its own semaphore, sized by that model's max_parallel (default 1 — fully serialized). Two requests against different models never wait on each other at all; within one model, calls overlap up to max_parallel — each overlapping call is still a full sequential decode sharing the box's CPU/GPU via the OS scheduler and torch's own intra-op thread pool, not a throughput multiplier, so raise it only after benchmarking on the target machine.

On top of per-model concurrency, max_queue bounds how many requests may be admitted (queued + running) across all models at once — once that many are admitted, further POST /generate calls get an immediate 503 (with Retry-After) instead of hanging on an unbounded wait, mirroring Ollama's OLLAMA_MAX_QUEUE backpressure. GET /health and GET /info remain responsive throughout regardless of queue depth.

A request whose client goes away (closes the connection, crashes, loses the network) is cancelled, streamed or not, so it doesn't hold its model and queue slots until it finishes. --max-generation-seconds cancels a generation that runs too long whatever the client does.

docs.title: Models
docs.text: midigpt ships pretrained checkpoints for three encoder families — yellow (yellow_medium, and the smaller, faster yellow_small), prism_medium, and expressive_medium — each trained on a different encoder configuration and loadable via InferenceEngine.from_pretrained. Choosing the right model depends on the kind of music you're working with and the generation mode you need.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Model num_bars_map Context (tokens) MaskBar Microtiming Velocity bins Download yellow_medium 4, 8 2048 no no 32 yellow_medium-final.safetensors yellow_small 4, 8 2048 no no 32 yellow_small-final.safetensors prism_medium 4, 8, 12, 16 4096 no no 32 prism_medium-final.safetensors expressive_medium 4, 8, 12, 16 4096 no yes 128 expressive_medium-final.safetensors

The yellow model conditions on: note density, min/max polyphony, and min/max note duration. prism and expressive support a wider set of attribute controls: key signature, pitch range, silence proportion, min/max note duration, note density (bar-level), min/max polyphony (bar-level), pitch class set (bar-level), and 18 genre groups. expressive additionally has NOMML (median metric depth) and piece-level switchable microtiming/velocity controls; prism does not.

Each attribute applies to melodic tracks, drum tracks or both: on yellow, note density is drum-only and polyphony and note duration are melodic-only; on prism and expressive, bar-level note density is drum-only and silence proportion applies to both. engine._analyzer.attribute_track_types() and GET /info (attribute_track_types) give the mapping for a checkpoint.

The weights are under the Metacreation Non-Commercial Research License (non-commercial research, including research-creation, and education), separately from the MIT-licensed code. They were trained on GigaMIDI v2.0.0.

InferenceEngine.from_pretrained(name) downloads the current checkpoint for that model name.

docs.title: Access tokens
docs.text:
When the model repo is gated, downloading a checkpoint needs a Hugging Face account that has accepted the license:

  1. Sign in at huggingface.co, open Metacreation/MIDI-GPT and accept the license.
  2. Create an access token (Settings → Access Tokens; "Read" is enough).
  3. Give it to midigpt, either way:
  4. run hf auth login once (stores the token for every tool that uses huggingface_hub), or
  5. set HF_TOKEN=hf_... in the environment.

InferenceEngine.from_pretrained(name, token="hf_...") and hf_token in the HTTP server's config file take a token directly. Prefer hf auth login or HF_TOKEN over putting a token on a command line or in a shared file.

A checkpoint is downloaded once; after that it loads from the cache (~/.cache/huggingface/hub/) even without a network connection or token.

docs.title: Yellow
docs.text:
The baseline checkpoint. Clean encoder, broad context window support (4 or 8 bars), works with any attention-based mask mode. A good default for most composition tasks.

engine = InferenceEngine.from_pretrained("yellow_medium")
# or load locally:
engine = InferenceEngine.from_checkpoint("yellow_medium-final.safetensors")

When to use: General-purpose melody and accompaniment generation. If you are not sure which model to pick, start here.

Mask mode: yellow does not have a MaskBar token — use mask_mode="attention" (or "attention_approx", "attention_skip", "remove").

docs.title: Prism
docs.text:
A general-purpose checkpoint trained on the same wide attribute set as expressive — key signature, pitch range, silence proportion, note duration, note density (bar-level), polyphony (bar-level), pitch class set (bar-level), and 18 genre groups — across the full range of context windows (4, 8, 12, or 16 bars). Unlike expressive, it uses standard 32-level velocity, does not emit microtiming/delta tokens, and has no switchable velocity/microtiming controls.

engine = InferenceEngine.from_pretrained("prism_medium")

When to use: General-purpose composition and infill when you want genre- or attribute-conditioned control and/or a longer context window (up to 16 bars), without the microtiming overhead of expressive.

Mask mode: prism does not have a MaskBar token — use mask_mode="attention" (or "attention_approx", "attention_skip", "remove").

docs.title: Expressive
docs.text:
A microtiming-aware checkpoint. The encoder emits delta offset tokens that capture note placement at sub-grid resolution, and uses 128 velocity bins (vs. 32 for the other models). It includes a nomml attribute control (median metric depth) to govern the degree of expressive timing vs. quantization. It also supports piece-level switchable controls for velocity and microtiming. This produces output that feels more "human" and less quantized.

When to use: When timbral and rhythmic nuance matters more than structural control — e.g. jazz, solo piano, or any music where expressive timing is essential.

Mask mode: expressive does not have a MaskBar token — use mask_mode="attention" or similar.

docs.title: Compatibility matrix
docs.text:
Which mask_mode values work with each model:

mask_mode yellow_medium / yellow_small prism_medium expressive_medium "attention" yes yes yes "attention_approx" yes yes yes "attention_skip" yes yes yes "remove" yes yes yes "token" no no no

Which model_dim values are valid:

model_dim yellow_medium / yellow_small prism_medium expressive_medium 4 yes yes yes 8 yes yes yes 12 no yes yes 16 no yes yes

docs.title: model_dim and context
docs.text:
model_dim is the number of bars in the model's context window — it is not a vocabulary or architecture dimension. See Concepts — The context window for a full explanation.

Pass a value from the model's num_bars_map. The session will raise a RequestValidationError if you pass a value that does not appear in the checkpoint's map.

# Valid for all models (4 or 8 bars)
InferenceConfig(model_dim=4, mask_mode="attention")
InferenceConfig(model_dim=8, mask_mode="attention")

# Valid for prism_medium and expressive_medium only (4, 8, 12, or 16 bars)
InferenceConfig(model_dim=12, mask_mode="attention")
InferenceConfig(model_dim=16, mask_mode="attention")

docs.title: Checkpoint format
docs.text:
By default, checkpoints are packaged as .safetensors files (format_version: 2) embedding the weights and metadata:

  • Weights: Stored natively in SafeTensors format.
  • Metadata: Stored inside the SafeTensors file header with the following keys:
  • format_version: "2"
  • arch: "gpt2"
  • config: A JSON string representing the model architecture configuration (e.g., n_embd, n_layer, n_head).
  • encoder_config: A JSON string representing the full encoder configuration (vocabulary domains, resolution, etc.).

load_checkpoint(path) is backwards-compatible and also accepts: * Legacy .pt packed-bundle files (format_version: 1) containing a pickled dict of weights, architecture, and encoder configuration. * A directory containing config.json + model.pt (legacy TorchScript representation).

docs.title: Real-time OSC Server
docs.text: The midigpt[realtime] extra adds a UDP OSC server for DAW and live-performance integration. The server listens for incoming note and bar events and streams generated notes back in real time.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
pip install "midigpt[realtime]"
midigpt-server --ckpt models/yellow_medium-final.safetensors --port 7400

Generation is triggered bar-by-bar via /midigpt/bar/end and runs on a dedicated background thread — the OSC listener never blocks.

docs.title: midigpt-server options
docs.text:
Flag Default Description --ckpt PATH — (required) Checkpoint to load (.safetensors or packed .pt) --host HOST / --port PORT 0.0.0.0 / 7400 UDP address to listen on --reply-port PORT sender's port Always send replies to this port --max_attempts N 3 Retry attempts per generation --model_dim N — Initial model_dim (also settable over OSC) --buffer N / --lookahead N — Initial buffer_bars / lookahead_bars (also settable over OSC) --gen_timeout SECONDS — Generation timeout; 0 = off (also settable over OSC) --log_level LEVEL INFO DEBUG, INFO, WARNING, ERROR

midigpt-listen [--host HOST] [--port PORT] prints every OSC message it receives, with no model: handy for checking what a client sends.

Studio UI: The browser-based studio is not included in the PyPI wheel. Clone the repository and run it from source with python -m midigpt.osc.studio.app --ckpt <checkpoint>. It requires a SoundFont file for audio playback — see src/python/midigpt/osc/studio/static/sf2/SOUNDFONTS.md.

docs.title: Session lifecycle
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    A["/midigpt/session/init"] --> B["Server replies\n/midigpt/capabilities"]
    B --> C["/midigpt/track/create\n(repeat per track)"]
    C --> D["/midigpt/session/start"]
    D --> E["Send notes + bar/end events\nin real time"]
    E --> F["/midigpt/generated/note\n(outbound, async)"]

docs.title: Inbound messages
docs.text:
Messages sent to the server:

Address Arguments Description /midigpt/session/init — Start a new session; server replies with /midigpt/capabilities /midigpt/session/start — Begin real-time generation /midigpt/session/end — End the current session /midigpt/track/create track_id, instrument, track_type Register a track (track_type: "melodic" or "drum") /midigpt/note track_id, pitch, velocity, onset, duration Push an incoming note event /midigpt/bar/end track_id, bar_index, ts_num, ts_den Signal end of a bar; may trigger generation /midigpt/param/set name, value Adjust a sampling parameter at runtime (see below) /midigpt/attr/set track_id, name, level Set a quantized attribute override for a track

docs.title: Outbound messages
docs.text:
Messages sent from the server:

Address Arguments Description /midigpt/capabilities JSON string Attribute names, sizes, and value labels for the loaded checkpoint /midigpt/generated/note track_id, pitch, velocity, onset, duration A generated note event /midigpt/generated/features JSON string Per-bar statistics (density, polyphony, etc.) /midigpt/prompt/state JSON string Per-bar context/mask/generate state snapshot

docs.title: Runtime parameters (/midigpt/param/set)
docs.text:
Adjust sampling behaviour without restarting the server:

Parameter Type Description temperature float Softmax temperature top_p float Nucleus sampling threshold mask_p float Anti-nucleus threshold mask_mode str Masking strategy ("attention", "token", etc.) model_dim int Context window in bars buffer_bars int Number of bars to buffer before triggering generation lookahead_bars int How far ahead to generate polyphony_hard_limit int Hard polyphony cap per bar (0 = off) silence_check int 1 = reject silent steps, 0 = allow novelty_check int 1 = reject identical outputs, 0 = allow

docs.title: Inference only
docs.text:
pip install "midigpt[inference]"

Pre-built wheels for CPython 3.10–3.14 on Linux (x86_64), macOS (x86_64 + arm64), and Windows (AMD64). No compiler needed.

On Intel Macs, midigpt[inference] needs Python 3.12 or older: PyTorch stopped publishing macOS x86_64 wheels after 2.2, so it installs with torch<2.3 and numpy<2.
